question: Under Warrant 1 Condition A in Table 4C-1, what are the 100-percent hourly volumes when the major street has two or more lanes and the minor street has one lane?
model_answer: Direct Answer: For Warrant 1, Condition A (Minimum Vehicular Volume), when the major street has two or more lanes and the minor street has one lane, the 100-percent volumes are 600 vehicles per hour on the major street (total of both approaches) and 150 vehicles per hour on the more critical minor-street approach (one direction only). Both of these volumes should exist for each of any 8 hours of an average day for the signal need to be considered under Condition A. Standards (mandatory): - "These major-street and minor-street volumes shall be for the same 8 hours for each condition; however, the 8 hours that are selected for the Condition A analysis shall not be required to be the same 8 hours that are selected for the Condition B analysis." Guidance (recommended): - The need for a traffic control signal should be considered if an engineering study finds that "the vehicles per hour given in both of the 100 percent columns of Condition A in Table 4C-1 exist on the major street and the more critical minor-street approach, respectively, to the intersection" for each of any 8 hours of an average day. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Table 4C-1, Condition A—Minimum Vehicular Volume, shows the row "2 or more" major-street lanes / "1" minor-street lane with 100% values of 600 vph on the major street and 150 vph on the more critical minor-street approach. [Image 3] The full-page view of Table 4C-1 confirms the same Condition A values (600 and 150) for the 2-or-more/1-lane configuration, with the footnote identifying the 100% column as the "basic minimum hourly volume." Citations: - Table 4C-1 (p.653) - Section 4C.02 Guidance §4 (p.653) - Section 4C.02 Standard §5 (p.653) - Section 4C.02 Support §1 (p.653) - Page 694
gold_answer: 600 vehicles per hour on the major street, total of both approaches, and 150 vehicles per hour on the more critical minor-street approach in one direction.
